actions: Modeled guard_epoch as ordinary claim/staging provenance rather than assuming it is an authoritative fence.
Executed a 72-scenario finite model over guard transition timing, ambiguous old publication response, exact staged-result contract, dedupe expiry, and guard-verifier availability.
Compared no epoch key, epoch key without sink check, client read-each, sink-time atomic check, fresh e2 reclaim with exact contract revalidation, and fail-closed behavior.
Persisted executable model, JSON result and checkpoint in the role-local namespace.
Rechecked the frozen root and role-config blobs after head movement; both remained identical, so no control change was adopted.

generic_residual_capability_boundary.minimum_generic_effect: Provide or enforce a server/sink invariant that atomically checks the current protected guard epoch at the authoritative effect boundary (or an equivalent protected atomic precondition); installing or changing that protected invariant is outside this CLEAN role.

termination.reason: Guard-epoch claim leaf completed. It separates claim provenance from authoritative sink fencing and leaves a nonempty multi-sink frontier.

exact_continuation: Next non-conflicting Phase-1 leaf: guard-epoch vector across multiple authoritative effect sinks. Model a parent requiring two effects whose sinks observe guard epochs asynchronously (e1/e1, e2/e1, e2/e2), one sink with durable idempotency and one with expiring dedupe, plus worker takeover and ambiguous response. Compare scalar parent guard epoch, per-sink epoch vector, sink-time atomic checks with a parent terminality certificate, and fail-closed serial integration. Test false parent terminalization, stale effect acceptance, duplicate effect, recoverability and staged-result reuse. Primary falsification: determine whether parent terminality may rely on a scalar epoch when sinks transition asynchronously, or must carry a vector/certificate proving each required effect under its own current authority and durable effect identity.
